evidence_map.basis_quote: A 10-day Israel-Lebanon ceasefire took effect in April 2026 after Trump said he had helped end another war. The Guardian reported that Israel’s security cabinet learned of the agreement from Trump’s social-media post, while Hezbollah heard about it from Iran’s ambassador to Lebanon. Both sides continued firing before the pause began. Israeli troops remained inside Lebanon after it took effect and fired on residents who approached; Hezbollah said it would respect the pause while keeping fighters ready. The arrangement did not resolve a border dispute dating to 2000 or the question of Hezbollah’s weapons. It was a temporary cessation of hostilities, not a comprehensive peace agreement.
